title: Research
text:
Quantitative Ecology · Conservation Bioacoustics · Ornithology




I study how bird communities respond to urban development across Stockton, California. Using passive acoustic monitoring and machine learning-based species identification, I am estimating species richness and occupancy in relation to vegetation structure and urban land use.
The Central Valley is one of North America’s most altered landscapes, having lost most of its historic wetlands, riparian forests, and grasslands. Those losses have contributed to widespread declines of habitat-specialist birds. This region also forms a large part of the Pacific Flyway bird migration route, so the habitat that remains is especially important for sustaining migratory species.
Species distributions are rarely resolved within a single city, so my project is producing localized data that citywide greening initiatives can act on.

title: About
text:
I was born and raised in Los Angeles, CA.
In my free time I enjoy trail running, rock climbing, mountaineering, birding, cooking, reading, and mushroom foraging.
I often post my adventures on mountain project, beak bagger, and strava, and cool critters, fungi, plants and such on iNaturalist and eBird.
